## Natural history notes

A small songbird characterized by its gray upperparts, pale underparts, black forehead, short stout bill, and distinct pointed crest. In Florida, it is found in hardwood hammocks, mixed forests, pine-oak woodlands, wooded neighborhoods, parks, and forest edges, especially where mature trees provide cavities for nesting. It feeds mainly on insects, spiders, seeds, nuts, and berries, often foraging actively on branches and trunks and sometimes joining mixed-species flocks.
